newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - positive tone ahead of FOMC.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - positive tone ahead of FOMC.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices ended Monday's session at the same place they started, largely ignoring Treasury and equities markets that reversed early losses.
"You can quote the market as somewhere between unchanged to 'unchanged and how,'" one market analyst said.
"It's a combination of the day before the Fed meets and Yom Kippur," a trader said, explaining the malaise. "You put those two together on a Monday and it spells boredom."

But the trader also noted that stocks and government bonds reversed early losses by the end of the day. Even though muni's barely took notice, "going into tomorrow, that's got to be somewhat positive," the trader said.

Tuesday's much anticipated meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee has market participants divided as to the likelihood of a rate hike. The Treasury long bond fell early Monday but was up 11/32 to yield 7.02 percent heading toward the New York close.
The Dow Jones industrial average also came back into positive territory after slipping badly at the start of the session. It ended at an unofficial record high of 5895.

Among the scarce secondary municipals out for the bid were Texas Turnpike Authority FGIC 5.0s of 2025, which were bid at a 5.83 percent yield, down two basis points from Friday's 5.85 percent. Cook County, Ill.'s FGIC 5-7/8s of 2022 were unchanged at 98-1/2.
But traders said none of the offerings were actually changing hands.
Debt futures ended higher, with the December municipal contract up 15/32 to 113-3/32 and the December T-bond up 11/32 at 108-3/32. The MOB spread was 160 ticks, four ticks wider than Friday.

Scheduled negotiated municipal bond sales are expected to total $218 million in 12 offerings for Tuesday, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group. The largest is a $55 million Wisconsin Health and Education Finance Authority revenue bond issue through Ziegler Securities.

Scheduled competitive municipal bond sales are expected to total $36 million in nine offerings for Tuesday. The largest on that list is a $7.8 million South Brunswick Township, N.J., general obligation issue set for 1100 EDT.
